analysis.title: TSMC (2330.TW) Earnings review: 3Q26 inline but 4Q26 GM came in slightly softer; AI demand outlook shows no signs of slowdown; reiterate Buy
key_insights: TSMC raised its 2026 revenue growth outlook to around 44% YoY in USD terms, from slightly above 40%, driven by AI/HPC demand.
3Q26 gross margin was 66.4%, down 1.3ppt QoQ on dilution from the initial N2 ramp. 4Q26 GM guidance is 65-67% (66.0% mid-point), 1.3ppt below GSe of 67.3% and in line with consensus of 66.1%.
Management called AI demand extremely robust with no sign of slowdown, far exceeding supply. It did not formally update the long-term AI accelerator revenue CAGR but said it will probably be higher.

Management cited four AI demand drivers: agentic AI lifting CPU demand (excluded from the AI accelerator definition), open-source model adoption, continued networking chip demand, and TSMC's own checks showing cloud providers are well prepared on US data center build and power.
N2 capacity will be more than double in 2027, the first time management has guided this. An additional N3 fab in Tainan was announced, with volume production in 1H28.
TSMC is evaluating Texas as an additional US site and is in discussion with one customer building Terafab on using that capacity. Management said its principle is to run the fab itself.

Overseas fab dilution is now expected near 2% for full-year 2026 (previously 2-3%). It is expected to widen to 3-4% later in the five-year period as more US fabs ramp. Management said there is 'no ceiling' for long-term profitability.
2026 CapEx guidance is unchanged at US$60-64bn. Management reiterated that 2026-2028 CapEx will be significantly higher than the prior three years and that revenue growth should outpace CapEx growth.
GS lowers GM estimates to 66.6%/66.8%/67.7% for 2026-2028E (from 67.2%/67.5%/67.8%). It raises 2026E EPS by 1.4% to NT$112.35, leaves 2027E at NT$150.01 (0.0%), and raises 2028E by 0.6% to NT$196.90.

Management is confident in its technology lead. High NA EUV adoption is planned for 2030, which it does not see as a disadvantage. Advanced packaging is in volume production at 5x reticle size, with 9x and 14x in development. A14 (volume production 2028) is expected to be a bigger node than N2, with customer engagement already above N2's at the same stage.
GS reiterates Buy with a 12m TP of NT$3,300 (22x P/E on 2027E EPS) and an ADR TP of US$660. This implies 35.2% upside for the local shares and 53.5% for the ADR.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterated Buy after the 3Q26 results on higher 2026 growth guidance and AI demand exceeding supply. The ADR TP of US$660 is unchanged and implies 53.5% upside from $430.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees TSMC's technology leadership and execution positioning it to capture structural AI/HPC growth, with a 3-year revenue CAGR of 38% in 2025-2028E.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported 10/15: revenue NT$1,494.2bn (US$46.72bn), up 17.6% QoQ and 50.9% YoY. Revenue was above the high end of USD guidance and above GSe/consensus by 0.8%/2.1%.

3Q26 reported EPS NT$29.43, up 8.0% QoQ and 68.7% YoY, above GSe (NT$29.07) by 1.2% and above consensus (NT$28.38) by 3.7%. Excluding the NT$2.24 one-off gain from the VIS disposal in 2Q26, EPS grew 18% QoQ.
3Q26 reported GM 66.4% was 1.1ppt below GSe (67.5%) and 0.1ppt below consensus (66.5%). Reported OpM was 58.7%, above the high end of the 56-58% guidance range.
3Q26 mix: N2 was 8% of wafer revenue (3% in 2Q26) and N3 was 33% (30%). Advanced nodes (7nm and below) were 79% (77%). HPC rose 22% QoQ to 68% of revenue, and smartphone rose 10% QoQ to 21%.
4Q26 company guidance: revenue US$52.3-54.3bn (+14% QoQ at the mid-point, at TWD/USD 31.8), GM 65-67% and OpM 56.5-58.5%. The revenue mid-point is well above GSe of +11.0% QoQ.
GS 2026E revenue is NT$5,620bn (+47.5% YoY). GS cut 4Q26E GM to 66.3% from 67.3% and 1Q27E GM to 66.3% from 67.5%.

trade_ideas.description: Buy TSMC (2330.TW) and the TSM ADR, 12m price target NT$3,300 / US$660
trade_ideas.rationale: Technology leadership and AI/HPC demand exceeding supply support a 22x target P/E on 2027E EPS.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker end-demand hurting utilization, slower node migration, an AI investment slowdown, poor yields, stronger competition eroding pricing, and FX or cost increases hurting margins.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in end-demand recovery hurting capacity utilization
Slowdown in AI investment lowering long-term semiconductor content growth
Poor yields or execution leading to worse-than-expected profitability
Stronger competition eroding ASP and profitability
Unfavorable FX or higher-than-expected costs weighing on margins
Overseas fab and N2 ramp dilution to gross margin

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue guidance and the 2026 growth outlook (~44%) are well above expectations. AI demand far exceeds supply, and management says there is 'no ceiling' for long-term profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 GM and 4Q26 GM guidance came in below GSe on steeper N2 ramp dilution and overseas fabs. Overseas dilution is expected to widen to 3-4% later in the five-year period.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowdown in AI investment, or N2 and overseas dilution widening faster than the company's guided 2% (2026) and 3-4% (later in the five-year period).
